recommendations.thesis: A tanker owner is short vessel supply and long voyage distance, and both moved hard the same way: VLCC Middle East-to-China day rates are near $498,000 against roughly $200,000 before the war and $20,000-60,000 in a normal market, while war-risk premiums have gone from 0.25% of hull value to 3-10%, so the owners still willing to transit Hormuz are paid extraordinary economics for the ones who will not. Frontline closed Friday at 46.12 after printing a 250-day high of 47.04 on 3.09M shares, above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (42.85 / 39.83 / 33.60), and it did that BEFORE the weekend strikes US equities have not yet traded. Verified tradeable on Robinhood: $10.27B market cap, NYSE-listed ordinary shares.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a war-premium trade at a one-year high after a 130% twelve-month run, and the exit is a headline, not a level: a ceasefire, a reopened strait or a de-risking of transits collapses spot VLCC rates far faster than they rose, and tanker equities de-rate on the rate print rather than on reported earnings. The 42.60 stop is 9.6% away and a genuine de-escalation gap can clear it overnight without ever filling near it. Short interest could not be fetched (api.nasdaq.com timed out twice), so one positioning input is missing. RED TEAM ADDITION: the 57.00 target is 6.03 ATR away, past the 6.0 ATR swing guide validation flagged, and at 21% above a 250-day high of 47.04 it sits in blue sky with no fetched resistance behind it - it is a measured-move extension of a trend, not a level. Pulling it to anything defensible below the high breaks the 2.16:1 ratio (55.00 gives 1.73:1), so read the ratio as resting on that extension. It is left standing rather than trimmed because the stop is the one thing in this report placed correctly - 42.60 is genuinely BELOW the 43.42-43.89 shelf, 2.79 ATR out - so the ratio was not manufactured from the risk side. Also unmentioned in the original: with XLE cut, this is now the report's only expression of the Iran/Hormuz driver, and the book still carries an open SPY short and a TLT short that lean on the same headline. A ceasefire hits all three at once. Size this as the whole oil bet, not as one of several.
recommendations.counter_argument: The whole move is already in the price - FRO is up 130% from a 250-day low of 20.47, sits 2% under its high, carries 71.4% bullish sell-side with zero sell ratings, and is being bought precisely because the news is loud. That is the textbook profile of a late cyclical chase, and spot tanker rates are the most mean-reverting series in shipping: $498,000 a day is not a level anyone underwrites as durable. Read the 6.91 trailing P/E as a warning rather than as support - a shipping company is cheapest on trailing earnings exactly at the peak of a rate cycle, and the 6.79% yield is largely variable dividends paid out of those peak earnings, so both numbers fall with the rate rather than cushioning it.

evidence.detail: Fetched relative strength: FRO +16.58% 1m, +31.13% 3m, +33.45% 6m against SPY +0.21% / +4.43% / +14.55% and XLE +10.14% / +11.08% / +13.24% - outperforming SPY on every window measured, and beating XLE too, so this is not just the oil trade in another wrapper. Sell-side is 3 strong buy, 2 buy, 2 hold, zero sell (71.4% bullish) and unchanged across four monthly periods, i.e. no deterioration to fade. Insider data: 0 open-market buys and 0 sells over six months - clean, unlike DHT (4 sells, $8.6M) and INSW (18 sells, $39.6M), which is why the trade is expressed in FRO.

Fetched bars: 250-day high 47.04 printed Friday 2026-09-04 on 3,088,344 shares against a rising base - SMA20 42.85, SMA50 39.83, SMA200 33.60, ATR14 1.6322. There is a real support shelf at 43.42-43.89 from the 08-28, 08-31 and 09-01 lows; the 42.60 stop sits below that shelf and below the SMA20, 2.79 ATR from entry, clearing the 2.0 ATR stock swing floor without being tightened to flatter the ratio.

The bear case is that this is a chase of a mean-reverting spot rate. The answer is that the rate move is measured rather than forecast - $498,000/day on the Gulf-to-Asia VLCC route is a printed fixture, not an estimate - and the mechanism driving it is a supply withdrawal that is getting worse, not better: owners are declining Hormuz transits and Iran has resumed attacking tankers, including two UAE supertankers. Mean reversion requires the transits to resume, which is precisely what Tehran's announced restricted maritime zone is designed to prevent. The trade is nonetheless sized at 2.5% and only exists above the high, because the counter-argument is strong enough that it should not be answered with size.

watchlist.note: Red team cut on stop placement, which is the one thing the ratio cannot survive. The idea names its own support shelf at 268.00-274.06 (the 08-31 and 09-01 lows, both re-fetched and confirmed) and then puts the stop at 277.00, ABOVE that shelf - so an ordinary retest of the base this four-session bounce launched from ends the trade. 09-01 alone traded 268.00-284.25, a 16.25-point range, so 22.85 points of risk is inside a single day's noise for this name. Place the stop where the evidence says it belongs, below 268.00, and the arithmetic collapses: risk 32.35 against reward 48.15 is 1.49:1, well under the 2.0 swing floor. At 273.90, just under the shelf, it is still only 1.86:1. The 2.11:1 that got this published exists only because the stop sits inside the structure. Validation already warned the stop was 2.38 ATR, under the 2.5 level where this book's stop-outs cluster. Conviction 4 was unpaid besides: CEG was 3, 3 and 2 on its three prior publications, the idea's own key_risk calls the positioning leg 'genuinely thin' (one insider buyer, sell-side 82.1% bullish and DETERIORATING at -3.1), and its own counter_argument declines to defend the valuation through a drawdown. The pending CEG BUY @ 272.00 from 2026-08-21 should still be CANCELLED - this cut does not revive it.
watchlist.trigger: A pullback that holds the 268.00-274.06 shelf and a target still 2:1 away from a stop placed BELOW it - roughly, an entry near 280 with the stop at 267 needs a target near 306. Or a second and third insider buyer, or realised PJM power prices printing nearer plan than NRG's $33.
